storm.summary_layperson: No storms anywhere nearby tonight — just a clear, calm, cold evening, with a frost advisory from 8 PM for inland areas.
storm.local_effect_blurb: Air and Sound water are both about 60°F at 4 PM, and the air drops well below the water after sunset — no marine-layer buffer at any point this evening, and none needed with no storms around.
storm.detail_html:
Regional picture: High pressure (about 1033 mb) is sitting over the area. The Upton radar shows no echoes to track, atmospheric instability is zero, and wind shear is under 7 kt — none of the ingredients for thunderstorms are present. The only alert is a Frost Advisory from 8 PM tonight to 9 AM Sunday, a cold-night hazard rather than a storm hazard.

Local effect: The cove’s usual protection is the cool Sound water putting a stable layer under incoming storms, which only works when the air is at least ~5°F warmer than the water. Today the gap is already gone: Sound water (Bridgeport Harbor) is 60.4°F and the cove air is about 60–61°F at 4 PM.

Through the evening: After sunset (6:00 PM) the air cools quickly while the Sound holds its temperature, so the air drops below the water — to about 54°F by 6 PM and 50°F by 7 PM. The protective gap never comes back. That doesn’t matter tonight, since there’s nothing for it to protect against.

Most likely outcome: Dry and clear for the cove and all surrounding towns. Inland spots will see frost; right on the water the Sound’s 60°F warmth should keep the shoreline a few degrees milder.

What would change the call: Nothing in the current data points to storms. A reading of zero instability under strong high pressure is about as settled as it gets.

wind.regime_label: Light gradient wind — no sea breeze, fading after sunset
wind.tactics_blurb: Drifter conditions: a fading 5 kt southwesterly at 5 PM swings toward the west and dies after the 6:00 sunset. Stay in the middle of the course, keep moving, and expect any racing to be over by about 6:30.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
Light gradient wind — no sea breeze in play. A sea breeze needs the land to be noticeably warmer than the water. Today the air–water temperature difference is only 0.4°F (cove air about 61°F, Sound water 60.4°F), well short of the ~5°F needed. Whatever wind there is comes from the weak large-scale flow around high pressure: well-sited airport stations average just 6.2 kt.

Now (4 PM): RYC reads SSW 7 kt gusting 8, with a 10-minute average of 5.2 kt. Bridgeport (SW 10) and New Haven (SW 6) agree on a light southwesterly along the Connecticut shore, but most stations just west and inland of the cove are close to calm and lean westerly. The forecast model has WNW 4–5 kt. Agreement between stations is poor (48%), which is typical when the wind is this light.

Through the window: Expect the southwesterly to soften to about 5 kt by 5 PM and swing toward the west as the sun goes down at 6:00. Once the sun is down the air cools quickly — it drops below the water temperature by about 6 PM — and the low-level air goes still. The 7–10 PM hours are near calm, with any wind drifting WNW–NW off the land. Those later hours are an estimate: the model run only reaches 7 PM.

Where the pressure is: In a southwesterly the wind is fairly even across the cove, if anything a touch stronger near the mouth. As it goes west, expect holes along the Connecticut shore. Once it turns northwest off the land it will be patchy everywhere. The middle of the course is the safest bet throughout. Look for dark patches on the water rather than relying on a side.

Racing impact: 4–5 kt at the start is drifter territory, still raceable for light-air specialists in dinghies. Below 3 kt after about 6:30, the race committee will probably shorten or abandon. If a race is on, the first start is the one to make. Dress warm: air temperature drops toward 50°F by 7 PM, with frost inland overnight.

data_caveats: Western Sound buoy 44040 offline (UConn ERDDAP fetch failed) — over-water wind and air temperature unavailable.
HRRR forecast hours f05–f12 unavailable; 20:00–22:00 wind rows are extrapolated from the 19:00 trend and post-sunset calming, not model output.
Sound water temperature from Bridgeport Harbor (BRHC3), not the western Sound buoy.
Cove wind (RYC SSW) and HRRR (WNW) disagree by ~95°; direction confidence is low in these light winds.
Frost Advisory in effect 8 PM–9 AM is a cold-weather alert, not a storm alert, so it does not raise the storm risk level.
